clue.text: Shower naked, holding cloth

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: naked means bare, uncovered
a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone takes a shower without clothes, clutching a flannel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' reads as washing, but it is the noun for a heavy volley, as in a shower of arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy, continuous outpouring of missiles or questions, which a shower of them describes.

clue.text: Mental image interrupted by extremely sexy companion

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into the middle of something, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a pic is a picture or image

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A daydream is broken into by a very attractive partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mental image' looks like one phrase, but 'Mental' alone is the definition and 'image' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychic describes things relating to the mind or soul, a standard sense of mental.

clue.text: Article about unknown American soldiers by the cut-off Israeli city

indicators.note: by means next to, joining the last piece on after the others
about here means turned around, so the article's letters run backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in grammar
Z is a mathematical unknown, as with x and y
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: cut-off means docked at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the word the, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A news item tells of unidentified US troops near a city cut off from the outside world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AN into NA; 'cut-off' docks THE to TH. The Royal Engineers, RE, are British soldiers despite the nearby 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazareth is a city in northern Israel, known as the town where Jesus grew up.

clue.text: Hit at random, unfortunately I fall

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is one where things went wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lashing out wildly admits they are going down.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is complete in the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To flail is to strike or swing wildly without aim, so blows land haphazardly.

clue.text: Rabbi's love for one prepared to learn

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or processed, so the letters are worked into a new order
for means in place of, so one letter stands in for another

parts.note: taken as written, the letters RABBIS
I is the Roman numeral for one
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A rabbi's devotion, kept for a single student, is ready to be taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts O (love) in place of I (one) in RABBIS, giving RABBOS, which 'prepared' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb knowledge is to take it in fully, which is what learning means.

clue.text: Minister starts to embarrass Rishi Sunak with a large U-turn?

parts.note: Rev, the Reverend, is a minister of religion

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only first letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of each of the three words
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation

explanation.surface: A government minister humiliates the Prime Minister with a big policy climbdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a politician, given Rishi Sunak, but it is a clergyman. The question mark flags that U-turn is used in its political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A political U-turn is a complete change of policy, a turning back on what was said before.

clue.text: Can drinking whiskey after French garlic ultimately yield gust from behind?

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so one set of letters swallows another
coming after means placed later in the sequence, fixing the order of two parts

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
ail is the French word for garlic
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A curious question about whether swigging whisky after eating garlic leads to wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a schoolboy joke about flatulence; whiskey spelt with an e signals the phonetic alphabet's W.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailwind blows in the same direction a vehicle or person is travelling, pushing from the rear.

clue.text: Writer's covering President endlessly, as before

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the writer's letters go round the president

parts.note: the writer is is I'M, the setter speaking

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Joe Biden was a US President

explanation.surface: An author is reporting on a president who never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' docks BIDEN to BIDE, and IM (Writer's, short for I'm) is 'covering' it. The answer is the Latin reference term found in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem, Latin for 'in the same place', is used in citations to point back to the source just cited.

clue.text: Appliances from Q's successor in antithesis of Bond film?

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the letter is enclosed

parts.note: Dr No is the first James Bond film; its opposite would be Dr Yes
R comes after Q in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Gadgets supplied by the next quartermaster in a Bond film parody.
explanation.walkthrough: Q is the gadget-maker in Bond films, so 'Appliances from Q' feels like one phrase; here Q is just the letter, followed by R.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair dryers and tumble dryers are household electrical machines, which is what appliances are.

clue.text: Manure always contains organic compound

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the letters sit within the words before it

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A fact about dung always having a certain chemical in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: manure does contain this compound, which helps hide the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a nitrogen-rich compound excreted in urine, the first organic substance made from inorganic materials.

clue.text: City traveller must circumnavigate to get back

indicators.note: to circumnavigate is to go all the way round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A traveller has to go around the world to make it home.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes start EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something lost is to regain or retrieve it, the same as getting it back.

clue.text: A gold plate conducting current with variable physical property

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to conduct is to carry or lead along, so one piece carries another inside it

parts.note: gilt is a thin layer of gold applied as plating
I is the symbol for electric current
algebra uses y as a variable

explanation.surface: A gold-coated plate carries electricity, with some changeable physical characteristic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all physics, and 'physical property' sounds like conductivity, but physical here means bodily.
explanation.definitionFit: Agility, nimbleness of movement, is a bodily quality, so it counts as a property of the physique.

clue.text: Death's edge about to slice one looking stunned

indicators.note: a slicing blade cuts into the middle, so these letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a gaper stares open-mouthed
a rim is an edge
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: The edge of a deathly blade is about to cut someone frozen in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Death stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grim Reaper is the traditional personification of death, a hooded skeleton carrying a scythe.

clue.text: Inappropriate looking dance, in retrospect

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: an inappropriate look

indicators.note: retrospect means looking backward, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Looking back, a dance move seems a bit unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inappropriate looking' seems to describe the dance, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a lecherous or sly glance, an improper way of eyeing someone.

clue.text: Allow doing away with European era voting rights

indicators.note: to do away with something is to get rid of it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: suffer in its old sense of permit
the letter taken out
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A call to scrap a Europe-era electoral system.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffer means allow in the biblical 'Suffer the little children'; drop its second E.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffrage is the right to vote in elections, as in the suffragettes' campaign for women's votes.

clue.text: Hotel program reader's to receive hot drink now at a discount

definitions.note: a time, defined by what happens in it

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one letter goes inside another piece

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an app is a computer program
addressing the reader, belonging to you
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A hotel app tells guests a hot drink is now cheaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot drink' looks like tea or coffee, but hot is only H and the definition starts at 'drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy hour is a period, usually early evening, when a bar sells alcohol at reduced prices.

clue.text: Don't be cruel talking about flavourless dessert

indicators.note: talking means speaking out loud, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: a plain ice is an unflavoured ice cream

explanation.surface: A plea not to mock someone's bland pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, the two words for an unflavoured ice run together into the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To play nice is to behave kindly and fairly towards others, the opposite of being cruel.

clue.text: Noisily eat cold late morning meal without starter

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: without starter means losing the first letter, as a meal without its first course

parts.note: brunch is a meal eaten late in the morning, blending breakfast and lunch

explanation.surface: Someone loudly munches a chilly brunch with no first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course of the meal but means its first letter, which is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To crunch food is to chew it with a loud crackling sound, as with crisps or raw carrots.

clue.text: Muse vaguely about a liberal prophet

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the a
vaguely means in an unclear or loose way, so the letters are loosely rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is idly musing on the subject of a liberal holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaguely' rearranges MUSE into SMUE, which goes 'about' A to make SAMUE, before L (liberal).
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel was the Old Testament prophet who anointed Saul and David as kings of Israel.

clue.text: Obstacle arranged to block coffin bearer

indicators.note: something that blocks sits inside a passage, so these letters are lodged within the other piece

parts.note: a bier is the stand a coffin rests on
arr. is the abbreviation for arranged, as on sheet music

explanation.surface: An obstruction is set up to stop a pallbearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coffin bearer' suggests a pallbearer, but the bearer is the frame that holds the coffin, and 'arranged' is an abbreviation, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is anything that blocks the way, so it is a synonym for an obstacle.

clue.text: Nothing to support idea propagated by books and film

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so this piece comes after the rest

parts.note: a meme is an idea or image spread from person to person
the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
zero, nothing, shaped like O

explanation.surface: No evidence backs an idea spread by books and cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like part of the list of media, but it is the definition, the 2000 Christopher Nolan thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Memento is a 2000 psychological thriller directed by Christopher Nolan, told in reverse order.

clue.text: Run boat's propeller and make a din

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an oar propels a rowing boat

explanation.surface: Starting a boat engine makes a loud racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propeller' suggests a motorboat's screw, but an oar is what propels a rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To roar is to make a loud deep noise, which is a way of making a racket.

clue.text: Hide in Magaluf with Eco novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hides away in a Spanish resort with an Umberto Eco book.
explanation.walkthrough: Magaluf is a Majorcan party resort and Umberto Eco an Italian novelist, so 'novel' looks like a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To camouflage something is to disguise it so it blends in and cannot be seen, which hides it.

clue.text: Rings husband's dropped — how clumsy!

indicators.note: something dropped has been let go, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: hoops are rings
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband has let the wedding rings fall, to everyone's dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after husband stands for has, as in husband has dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation people make after a minor accident or blunder, expressing embarrassment at clumsiness.

clue.text: Bird ascending east German mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the order is reversed

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation
Berg is German for mountain

explanation.surface: A bird flies up an eastern Alpine peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers both pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving waterbird with lobed toes, such as the great crested grebe.

clue.text: Newton with true confusion concerning particle

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

indicators.note: confusion means disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
on means concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton is genuinely puzzled about some subatomic particle.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton is the physicist in the surface, but in the wordplay it is the unit of force, symbol N.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is an uncharged subatomic particle found in the nucleus of an atom.

clue.text: Plain, quiet, less stuffy royal brought to the fore

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

indicators.note: royal stands for R, as in ER, and brought to the fore says that letter moves to the front

parts.note: airier means better ventilated, so less stuffy

explanation.surface: A quiet, less formal member of the royal family has been pushed into the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal' names the letter R, as in the ER of the monarch's cipher, and 'royal brought to the fore' moves that R from the end of the less-stuffy word to its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open area of flat grassland, especially in North America, so it is a plain.

clue.text: Fearless journalist to trade leaders: show restraint

indicators.note: to trade means to exchange, so each word gives up its first letter for the other's

parts.note: bold means brave or fearless

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the two words, the ones being swapped

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a disparaging term

explanation.surface: A brave reporter tells business chiefs to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trade leaders' sounds like business bosses, but it tells BOLD and HACK to exchange their first letters, giving HOLD and BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back is to refrain or keep oneself in check, which is exercising restraint.

clue.text: Briefly put off by court notice

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off

explanation.surface: A short postponement is announced in a court bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' looks like a noun for a written announcement, but it is the verb: to spot. DETER, 'Briefly', is DETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To detect something is to discover or notice its presence, often something hidden.
